porto.attribution: Moreira-Matias et al. (2013), Taxi Service Trajectory - Prediction Challenge, ECML PKDD 2015, UCI Machine Learning Repository, DOI 10.24432/C55W25.
porto.selection: First 1000 source-order complete-GPS trips with at least 3 valid samples starting on the first qualifying UTC day (2013-07-01); paths over 5000 samples excluded as a browser payload bound.
porto.hashScope: Downloaded ZIP prefix only, not the entire training archive. Stream chunk size is fixed at 65536 bytes after the header.
changes: Removed source trip, taxi and customer identifiers
Excluded incomplete and invalid paths with counts
Derived waypoint times using documented 15-second cadence
Added zero altitude only as a Kepler rendering placeholder
warnings: A source-order first-day subset is not representative of all Porto demand
GPS observations are 15 seconds apart; movement between them is interpolated
Altitude was not measured and is encoded as 0 solely for the rendering format
DAY_TYPE is known to be wrong in the source and is omitted
Elapsed sampled duration is derived from sample count, not an independent trip-meter measurement

usgs.attribution: U.S. Geological Survey, Earthquake Catalog. Historical January 2024 snapshot, magnitude 1 and above.
changes: Flattened Point geometry and event properties
Preserved depth in kilometers below the surface
Normalized epoch-millisecond times to UTC ISO timestamps
warnings: Historical catalog snapshot, not live reporting; catalog revisions can change counts
One polar event beyond Web Mercator latitude limits is excluded from this map only; its source coordinates are valid.
Counts show catalog events, not hazard, risk or probability
Catalog detection coverage and completeness vary geographically
Magnitude is logarithmic and is not a linear energy or density weight
Depth is kilometers below the surface, not positive altitude

census.license: U.S. Census Bureau employee-created public information
census.attribution: U.S. Census Bureau, 2024 Cartographic Boundary File, State and Equivalent Entities, 1:20,000,000; converted to WGS84 GeoJSON.
changes: Converted NAD83 shapefile to WGS84 GeoJSON with pyproj
Rounded display coordinates to six decimal places
Converted ALAND/AWATER square meters to square kilometers
warnings: Generalized display boundaries, not navigation or parcel geometry
Land area is the measured color value; this is not population or population density
Includes Alaska, Hawaii, District of Columbia and Puerto Rico; a global fit is appropriate to the complete dataset
Analysis conclusions are the portfolio author's, not a Census endorsement
Whole-period event counts, not rates or probability
Cell sizes vary; these values have no exposure denominator
Cells whose centroids exceed Web Mercator latitude limits are omitted and counted in the manifest
No time playback is claimed for this aggregated table

selection.name: Western US region
selection.description: Select January 2024 catalog events with latitude 25..50 and longitude -126..-100, inclusive; aggregate these selected observations to S2 level 7.
selection.reason: A regional example avoids cross-antimeridian S2 cell drawing limitations in the installed Kepler 2.2 renderer.

warnings: Regional example only: the inclusive Western US bounding box is latitude 25..50 and longitude -126..-100; this is not a global S2 event map.
Selected 2716 of 8945 mapped catalog events; 6229 observations outside this region are not invalid or missing.
The geographic box also includes neighboring parts of Canada and Mexico and offshore events; it is not a US administrative-boundary filter.
A regional example avoids cross-antimeridian S2 cell drawing limitations in the installed Kepler 2.2 renderer.
Whole-period event counts, not rates or probability
Cell sizes vary; these values have no exposure denominator
Cells whose centroids exceed Web Mercator latitude limits are omitted and counted in the manifest
No time playback is claimed for this aggregated table

selection.regionMeaning: Declared showcase bounding box, not an administrative city boundary
selection.speedMethod: Haversine great-circle displacement with Earth radius 6371000m divided by the observed 15-second interval
selection.qualityRule: Exclude the whole original trip when any consecutive observations imply speed above the threshold; this is a showcase quality flag, not proof of impossible travel
selection.windowRule: Scan UTC-minute-aligned 30-minute windows from the first source UTC midnight through the last observed time; keep only existing observations inside the inclusive window
selection.regionRule: Discard the whole clipped segment if any retained vertex is outside the inclusive region box; never remove intermediate points or bridge gaps
selection.ranking: Most retained observed positions after quality and region filters; earliest window wins a tie
selection.concurrencyMeaning: Selected recorded segments underway during [first retained observation, last retained observation), not all Porto taxis

fieldMeanings.originalFields: All original scalar trip attributes are preserved unchanged, including full-trip started_at, ended_at, duration_seconds and endpoint coordinates
fieldMeanings.segmentFields: segment_* time, duration and coordinates describe only the retained observed segment; clipping flags say whether its original beginning or end lies outside the selected time window
fieldMeanings.geometry: A contiguous slice of unchanged original four-coordinate GPS observations, with their existing timestamps and zero-altitude rendering placeholder
fieldMeanings.dispatch_type: Original request channel: central dispatch, taxi stand or street hail; not vehicle or job status

warnings: Selected urban morning showcase from a source-order first-day sample; not all Porto demand, a live fleet, or a representative traffic study
87 of 161 displayed records are time-clipped trip segments; their visible endpoints are not necessarily pickup or drop-off locations
The 150km/h implied-speed threshold is a documented visual quality flag, not a validated finding about travel or every possible GPS error
The region box is a display selection, not a Porto administrative boundary; observations outside it remain valid source data
No GPS position or timestamp is fabricated; screen movement interpolates the source's 15-second observations
Original full-trip and origin/destination assets remain available and unchanged

policy: No paid API or data credential is used
Raw personal/customer/taxi identifiers from Porto are omitted
All displayed results must retain source/subset and inferential limitations
